issueSummary: Three developments worth your time. One needs a legal read.

developments.headline: DOL proposes cybersecurity program requirements for employee benefit plans
summary: Would require plans to adopt, document, and annually review a written cybersecurity program and report certain incidents to DOL within 72 hours.
The proposal would reach health and welfare plans, including multiemployer funds and their service providers, creating new governance, vendor, and breach-notification duties.
developments.confidenceNote: The legal status and comment date were confirmed against the primary material.
developments.affected: Multiemployer health and welfare plans and their service providers
developments.action: Confirm whether existing governance and vendor-review materials would need revision.
developments.timing: Attorney assessment before the comment deadline
developments.completion: Research assignment prepared for attorney review.
developments.passage: Plans would be expected to maintain a documented program proportionate to their systems, data, and service-provider relationships.

developments.headline: ACA Forms 1094/1095 reporting deadline
summary: Applicable large employers and self-funded plans must file Forms 1094-C and 1095-C with the IRS and furnish statements to individuals.
developments.confidenceNote: The date and filing requirement were matched to current IRS instructions.
developments.affected: Applicable large employers and self-funded health plans
developments.action: Confirm the filing calendar and responsible service provider.
developments.completion: Deadline review item prepared for paralegal confirmation.
developments.passage: The filing obligation applies to applicable large employers and providers of minimum essential coverage, subject to the governing instructions.

developments.headline: Ninth Circuit to reconsider MHPAEA standard of review
developments.status: Decision pending · Briefing schedule not set
summary: The court granted rehearing en banc in a MHPAEA matter challenging application of the “de novo unless deferential” standard.
developments.uncertainty: Uncertain — the briefing schedule has not been set.
developments.confidenceNote: The procedural development is clear, but its eventual effect on plan administration remains open.
developments.affected: Health plans defending MHPAEA benefit determinations in the Ninth Circuit
developments.action: Monitor the briefing schedule and eventual standard articulated by the en banc court.
developments.completion: Monitoring follow-up prepared for attorney review.
developments.passage: The en banc court will reconsider the framework used to review the challenged mental-health benefit determination.
developments.authorityLabel: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
